headline: Best-recovered week of the block at near-peak volume (72.8km) — HRV/RHR kept improving through the same load that tipped them over in early August, and the first continuous HM-pace block (20T+15H) executed cleanly on pace and achilles. Hold the plan.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 23 August 2026

**Week of 17–23 August. Week 5 of the Cheltenham build. 28 days to race day.**

## Following up from Friday's ACWR question

You asked on Friday's form why the ACWR wasn't reading at the top of OPTIMAL
after the weekend, as I'd suggested it might. That got answered directly
this afternoon (see `coach_reply` on last week's review), so I won't re-run
it in full here — short version: the prediction was off, not the data.
Acute load moved into OPTIMAL but only to the bottom of the band (0.9) rather
than the top, because chronic load (957) is now higher than it was during
the comparable 8–9 Aug weekend (925) — the two heaviest weeks of the block
are still rolling through that 28-day window, so the same acute effort
produces a smaller ratio. That's a higher fitness baseline showing up in the
arithmetic, not a fault. This week's numbers bear that read out: recovery
held through the biggest single quality jump of the block (see below), which
is what you'd expect if the low-in-band reading was reassuring rather than a
flag.

## How the week actually went

| | This week | Last week | Week before |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volume | 72.8 km | 67.9 km | 73.7 km |
| Runs | 6 | 5 | 6 |
| Elevation | 427 m | 317 m | 384 m |
| Quality time | 142 min | 141 min | 159 min |
| Easy share | 59% | 58% | 55% |
| Efficiency | 1.478 | 1.425 | **1.498** |
| Avg HRV | 40.0 | 38.6 | — |
| Avg RHR | 47.3 | 47.9 | — |
| Avg sleep score | 86.9 | 86.1 | — |

Plan was 70 km (rest, 8, 13, 7, 5, 16, 21). You ran 72.8 km — the ~2.8 km
over comes almost entirely from the two quality sessions running slightly
long against their targets (14.01 km vs 13, 17.02 km vs 16), which is normal
session-shape variance, not drift.

The session-by-session detail, from `session_detail.json` (all three quality
sessions this week were structured — reps and recoveries read straight off
the watch's own workout markers, not inferred):

- **Wed 19 Aug (intervals):** 5x1200m, target 3:44/km, actual mean **3:41/km**,
  spread 1.3 sec/km — about as even as a rep session gets — drift +0.4
  sec/km (flat, no fade). Note: "Felt strong... could have done more," RPE 6.
  Already covered in Wednesday's mid-week reply: a comfortable execution of
  a 10K-effort session isn't under-loading, it's the session doing what it's
  designed to do. Nothing new to add — the data this week confirms it wasn't
  a one-off, since the following two sessions held up fine too.
- **Sat 22 Aug (tempo, bumped to 20T+15H per your Friday 21 Aug request):**
  block 1 (20min threshold) at **3:50/km** — exactly on the 3:50 target.
  Block 2 (15min HM pace) at **3:55/km** against a 3:54 target — essentially
  on the money. The +5.6 sec/km "drift" the raw numbers show is the two
  different prescribed paces, not fatigue — read block-to-block, not as one
  continuous effort. Note: "Run fine... very slight achillies on warm down
  but still below a 1/10." RPE 6, achilles logged 0.
- **Sun 23 Aug (long, today):** 21.03 km at 4:37/km, HR 143 — inside the
  4:36–4:59/km band. Decoupling **1.94%**, clean (no unreliable flags), at
  88.4 analysed minutes — the longest steady run in the decoupling series to
  date. First half 4:32/km at 141.9 HR, second half 4:38/km at exactly the
  same HR — that's about as flat an aerobic profile as this dataset has
  produced, on the biggest weekend load of the block. Note: "Chatty run...
  easy day, speed only fluctuated in rises and downhills."

Net effect: on-target on every planned session (`on_target_pct: 100`), the
first continuous HM-pace running of the build executed cleanly on both
counts (pace and achilles), and the peak long run held its aerobic
efficiency at 21 km. That's a genuinely strong week to sit right before the
taper conversation starts.

## How he's coping — data and his own words

This is the more important story than the ACWR question. This week's volume
(72.8 km) sits almost exactly where the 3–9 Aug week did (73.7 km) — the
week that tipped HRV baseline 43.9→36.3 and RHR baseline 46.7→48.7 and
triggered a correction. This time, at essentially the same load, recovery
kept improving: avg HRV **38.6→40.0**, avg RHR **47.9→47.3**, sleep score
**86.1→86.9**, sleep duration **7.8→8.2 hrs**. Same volume, opposite
direction. Two things explain it, both already flagged in this week's
mid-week replies: chronic load is higher now (a real fitness gain, not an
artefact), and this week's quality was spread one session per type across
seven days rather than bunched the way early August was. The plan is
adapting to a genuinely fitter athlete, which is exactly what a build is
supposed to do.

The two isolated low mornings this week (HRV 33 on the 22nd, both explained
by logged alcohol confounders, RHR and sleep normal both times) fit the
confounder pattern the brief describes — explained, resolved within a day,
no trend. No action needed on either.

## Achilles

0 on every day this week. One note worth asking about directly: Saturday's
tempo carried "very slight achillies on warm down but still below a 1/10" —
the first achilles mention since early August, and it landed on the first
continuous HM-pace block of the build, which is exactly the kind of new
stimulus your history says to watch. I asked about it directly in
Saturday's mid-week reply — specifically whether it looked anything like the
old pattern (stiffness in the first steps, an ache from sitting) or was just
normal end-of-session fatigue — and haven't had an answer yet; today's note
doesn't mention it recurring, which is reassuring, but it's still an open
question rather than a closed one. Please answer that one directly, even if
the answer is "nothing since, felt fine" — that's the kind of thing that
should be closed out explicitly, not assumed.

## Heat

Milder week than the previous three — Wednesday's intervals ran in 22.1°C
(moderate), Saturday's tempo in 21.0°C (moderate), Sunday's long in 23.3°C
(moderate). No breathing complaints in any note. Next week's forecast turns
warm again through Mon–Thu (24–26°C, "high" heat_risk each day) before
cooling for the weekend (19–20°C) — worth having Symbicort/salbutamol
routine sharp for Tuesday's intervals session if the forecast holds.

## Efficiency trend

1.426 → 1.471 → 1.498 → 1.425 → **1.478** this week. Same read as last
week's dip, in reverse: easy pace ran 4.96 min/km against last week's 5.30,
both inside the prescribed 4:48–5:11/km easy zone but at different ends of
it. The efficiency number moved with pace discipline within the zone, not
with a genuine fitness step. Zoomed out, the underlying trend since the June
base week (1.219 → 1.478) is still the real signal, and it remains a clear,
genuine gain — this week's number doesn't add new evidence either way.

## Race countdown

28 days to Cheltenham (4.0 weeks). Prediction unchanged at **1:22:23**
(range 1:20:09–1:24:37) against your 1:22–1:23 target. Remaining key
sessions: 2 tempo, 3 intervals, 2 long. Taper starts 10 September — 2.5
weeks of loading left after this week.

## Recommendation: **hold**

Next week (24–30 Aug) is already the right shape: rest, easy 8, intervals 13
(6x1km @ 3:44/km), easy 7, easy 5, tempo 17 (20min threshold + 20min at HM
pace — the full goal-pace block, second step of the progression you asked
for on the 21st), long 21 (peak long run, **last 5km at HM pace**). That's
71 km — essentially flat against this week's 72.8, which is the right call
two weeks from the key 5 Sep session and 2.5 weeks from taper: this week
proved the volume and the new HM-pace stimulus are both being tolerated, not
that there's room to keep stacking increases on top of each other before the
taper conversation starts. No changes to the plan.

One thing to close out before Wednesday, not a plan change: whether
Saturday's achilles note was anything like the old pattern or just normal
fatigue.

coach_reply:
Shep — good session, and worth a proper look rather than a one-line "nice work."

One caveat up front: this form submission runs the forms-only pipeline, so today's run hasn't gone through Garmin yet — no lap splits, HR or exact volume in `session_detail.json` or `garmin_activities.json`. I'm reading this entirely off your note, and I'll give it the full rep-by-rep treatment once the data's through (certainly by Sunday's review).

On what you did report: 6x1km at 3:44/km target, and you were slightly ahead throughout despite deliberately trying to hold back to hit it exactly. That's not a one-off — 12 Aug was the same session, same 3:44 target, and it came in at 3:40 avg. Two sessions at the same prescribed 10K-effort pace, both landing quicker than written even when you're trying not to, is a pattern: the target's a touch conservative for where your fitness actually is right now, not that you're pacing loosely. Combined with RPE 7 (normal for this session, not elevated) and achilles at 0, that's a clean, well-controlled execution — not one where you emptied the tank to make it happen.

The heat is the part I'd flag properly rather than wave through. 30°C is meaningfully hotter than any hard session this build — for comparison, 19 Aug's intervals were 21°C, 22 Aug's tempo was 14°C, and today's forecast max was 26.1°C, so you were running in something noticeably hotter than even the forecast said. That's exactly the "high heat risk + hard session" combination the brief treats as a genuine flag, and on the numbers you've given me it passed clean — no breathing complaint in the note, RPE in the normal band, achilles 0. But I'd rather ask than assume: any chest tightness or breathing awareness at all, even mild? You're not on the daily preventer right now, and this is the hottest hard session you've logged this block — if there was anything, even minor, that's useful information for the Symbicort-restart conversation you've already flagged wanting to have with your GP before Cheltenham. If there was genuinely nothing, that's a good data point in itself.

One more thing worth noting for the record: the gel during warm-up. Every gel you've logged so far has been mid-way through an easy long run — this is the first one attached to a quality session, and gastric emptying at 10K effort is a different environment to easy-pace running. No GI mention in your note, which is reassuring, but flagging it because carbs/hour and caffeine at effort are still unquantified per the brief, and Cheltenham's race pace is closer to this effort than to a long run. Worth a line in future notes on how the stomach felt when you fuel around anything harder than easy.

Nothing here changes the plan. This is a strong data point that the build's still being tolerated well, not a reason to add anything on top of it two and a half weeks from taper. Rest of the week runs as written: easy 7 Thu, easy 5 Fri, tempo 17 (20T+20H, the full goal-pace block) Sat, long 21 — peak long run, last 5km at HM pace — Sun.

conversation.athlete_thoughts: You were expecting the ACWR to be right at the top end of the green after today... It's only just in the green at the bottom end. Just trying to understand it
conversation.coach_reply:
Shep — fair to push on this again, the review's version was buried in a wall of numbers. Here's the direct version.

Today's Garmin ACWR is 0.9: acute load 924, chronic load 957 — bottom of the OPTIMAL band (0.8–1.3), not the top. The comparison that matters is 9 August, the last time chronic load sat this high (925, essentially identical to today's 957) — but acute load that day was 1,309, a third higher than today's 924. That was the weekend that tipped you into overreaching and triggered the correction two reviews ago.

So the difference isn't that this week loaded light — 72.8 km is close to peak — it's that chronic load (your rolling fitness baseline) has climbed from 925 to 957 since early August, which is a genuine gain, and a higher chronic load needs a bigger acute number to produce the same ratio. On 9 August, 1,309 acute against 925 chronic gave you 1.4 (HIGH). Today, 924 acute against the now-higher 957 chronic gives 0.9. Same-ish acute effort, higher denominator, lower ratio — arithmetic, not a training problem.

To see ACWR back near the top of OPTIMAL at this chronic level you'd need an acute week noticeably bigger than this one — which is a description of a fitter athlete carrying more load comfortably, not something to chase. Nothing here changes the hold: this reading is confirmatory, not a flag.

Shep — good, that closes it out. No stiffness in the first steps, no ache from sitting, nothing since Saturday — that's not the old pattern, it's what a first exposure to continuous HM-pace running looks like on a tendon that's been asymptomatic for months: a small transient signal after a genuinely new stimulus, gone within a day. Worth asking rather than assuming, and worth you volunteering it unprompted — keep flagging anything like that the moment it shows up, not after.

Nothing changes. The hold stands and next week runs as written: rest Mon, easy 8 Tue, intervals 13 (6x1km @ 3:44/km) Wed, easy 7/5 Thu/Fri, tempo 17 (20T+20H, the full goal-pace block) Sat, long 21 with the last 5km at HM pace Sun. That's the second continuous HM-pace exposure of the build — same watch, same question if anything recurs, but a one-off with no change in load doesn't need a plan change on its own.

One practical note: Wednesday's intervals (not Tuesday — small correction on my part) lands in the warm patch forecast for Mon–Thu (24–26°C, high heat risk). Symbicort 20 min before, salbutamol 15 before, same as race protocol, if that heat holds.

Shep — noted, thanks for flagging it. Today's `computed_data.json` confirms it: HRV, sleep score, sleep duration and achilles score for last night are all null, because there's nothing for the watch to have recorded. RHR (48) and body battery (86) are still there — those come from the watch being on you at some point today rather than needing a full night, so they're not affected the same way.

Nothing to correct and nothing to read into it. It's a gap, not a low reading — different from a night where the watch was worn and HRV genuinely dropped. I won't count today against the 7-day HRV/RHR baselines as if it were a real data point, and today's a scheduled rest day anyway, so there's no session to misjudge off the back of it. If you're not wearing it again tomorrow night before Tuesday's easy 8, same treatment — just say so and I'll read around the gap rather than into it.

No change to the plan. Wednesday's intervals (6x1km @ 3:44/km) still lands in the forecast warm patch (24–26°C, high heat risk) — Symbicort 20 min before, salbutamol 15 before, as flagged Saturday.
